messageValues.message:
You are an email classifier for a PERSONAL VIRTUAL ASSISTANT whose duties are: calendar scheduling, email drafting on the user's behalf, personal/professional correspondence, and task reminders.

ANY email NOT relevant to those duties — promotional / marketing emails, customer-support chatbot inquiries (belong to a different system), cold outreach / sales pitches, phishing / scams / lottery / unsolicited offers — must be classified as `spam`. Pure informational digests go to `newsletter`.

Return ONLY a JSON object (no markdown, no extra text) with EXACTLY these fields:

- "category": one of "urgent", "normal", "newsletter", "spam".
- "action": one of "reply", "draft", "file", "ignore".
- "summary": 1-2 sentence neutral summary.
- "suggested_reply": the COMPLETE, ready-to-send reply text if action is reply/draft, otherwise "". NO PLACEHOLDERS: never output bracketed placeholders such as [Sender Name], [Your Name], [Date], [Company]. Greet the sender by the real name parsed from the From field above; if no usable name is available, open with just "Hi," or "Hello,". Do NOT add any signature or sign-off name line (no "Best, <name>", no "[Your Name]") — end with the final sentence of the message body. Every bracketed placeholder must be replaced with a real value or removed.
- "confirmation_required": boolean — true for urgent/normal, false for newsletter/spam.
- "has_calendar_action": boolean — true ONLY if the email explicitly proposes a SPECIFIC date+time for a meeting/event the user should put on their calendar. False for vague mentions or past events.
- "event_title": string — the event title to put on the calendar if has_calendar_action, else "".
- "event_start_iso": string — ISO 8601 timestamp WITH timezone offset for Europe/Sarajevo (e.g. 2026-05-12T14:00:00+02:00) if has_calendar_action, else "".
- "event_end_iso": string — same format if has_calendar_action; if duration unspecified, default to start + 1 hour, else "".

Return ONLY the JSON object.

parameters.content:
# Email VA - Proactive Monitor

## Purpose
Proactively monitors the personal-assistant Gmail inbox for new unread messages, classifies each one with an LLM, and routes it down an action-specific branch. For emails that warrant a reply it drafts a ready-to-send response, checks the calendar when a meeting is proposed, and asks the user for explicit Telegram approval before anything is sent or booked. Newsletters and spam are labeled/notified automatically, and every branch logs its outcome to Google Sheets.

## How it works
- Gmail Trigger polls every minute for unread mail from the owner.
- Classify Email (LLM chain on Google Vertex AI, Gemini 2.5 Flash) returns JSON with category (urgent/normal/newsletter/spam), action (reply/draft/file/ignore), summary, suggested_reply, confirmation flags, and optional calendar fields (has_calendar_action, event_title, event_start_iso, event_end_iso).
- Parse Classifier Output (Code) cleans/validates the JSON, falls back to safe defaults on parse failure, and re-attaches the original email's from/subject/threadId/messageId.
- Action Router (Switch) splits on action into four branches: draft, reply, file, ignore.
- draft and reply both feed Has Calendar Action?: if a specific date+time was proposed it runs Check Availability (Google Calendar getAll over the proposed window), otherwise it skips to Build Approval Card.
- Build Approval Card (Code) recomputes slot_free / conflict_summary from the busy results and composes a Telegram card showing From, Subject, Category, the proposed reply, and (when applicable) the event details with a free/conflict notice.
- Telegram Approval sends a double-confirmation approve/reject card to the configured Telegram chat with a 24-hour wait.
- Approved? branches on the approval. On approve: Has Calendar Action? (Post-Approve) decides between the calendar path and a plain reply. With a calendar action, Slot Free? either creates the event (Create Calendar Event -> Send Reply -> Notify Combined Success) or, on conflict, builds a conflict card (Build Conflict Card -> Notify Conflict -> Create Draft (Conflict)) so nothing is sent. Without a calendar action it just sends Send Reply (Simple).
- On reject/timeout: Create Draft Reply saves the response to Gmail Drafts instead of sending.
- file (newsletters) -> Notify: FYI Only on Telegram -> Apply Newsletter Label -> Mark Read (FYI).
- ignore (spam) -> Apply SPAM Label -> Mark Read (Spam).
- Every terminal branch marks the original message as read and appends an outcome row to Google Sheets via dedicated Prepare Log Code nodes.

## Triggered by
Gmail Trigger polling every minute for unread emails from the owner.

## Calls (sub-workflows)
- None. There are no executeWorkflow nodes; all logic runs inline within this workflow.

## Reads/writes
- Gmail: reads new unread mail via Gmail Trigger; replies in-thread (Send Reply, Send Reply (Simple)); creates drafts (Create Draft Reply, Create Draft (Conflict)); marks messages read across all branches; applies SPAM and Newsletter labels.
- Google Calendar (the assistant's Google Calendar): Check Availability reads busy times over the proposed event window; Create Calendar Event books the meeting after approval with no conflict.
- Telegram (the configured Telegram chat): Telegram Approval sends the double-confirmation approval card (24h wait); Notify: FYI Only, Notify Combined Success, and Notify Conflict send status messages.
- Google Sheets: appends outcome rows to tab `VA_Email_Log` (continueOnFail enabled).
- LLM: Google Vertex Chat Model powers the Classify Email chain.

## Running large test batches — auto-answering the approval gate
The `Telegram Approval` node is a `sendAndWait` node: it PAUSES the run until a human taps Approve/Reject in Telegram (24h timeout). Fine for live use, but for a 200-email test batch every run would hang on a manual tap.

To auto-answer it, branch the approval to an **Execute Sub-workflow** node calling **`Test Auto-Responder (Email VA Approval Simulator)`** — the simulator built for exactly this workflow:
- Execute-Workflow-Trigger (passthrough) → Code node returning a weighted-random verdict: 45% accept / 45% reject / 10% ignore (its target distribution over 200 cases).
- Output matches `sendAndWait`: `{ data: { approved: true|false }, decision, ignored }`, so the existing `Approved?` IF (which reads `data.approved`) works unchanged.
- Inline call → returns instantly, no webhook wait, so the whole batch runs unattended.

Recommended wiring: add a `Test Mode?` IF before the gate — Test Mode = true → Execute Sub-workflow (auto-responder); false → the real `Telegram Approval` (kept on the False branch). For deterministic outcomes, replace the simulator's `Random Decision` with a fixed `approved:true`, or read the expected verdict from the test row.
